title: AdapterMsg
description:
Anything crossing an adapter socket in either direction.

Requests carry an `op`; replies carry `ok`. The variants are tried in this order and their `op` vocabularies are disjoint.

AgentMount.description: Where an agent plugin attaches itself within the role.

pid.description: Process id, used for probe cross-checks on the local machine.

AgentPhase.description: Agent-side lifecycle fact: the agent dimension of a session, the word the ledger column stores, and the word the wire projection carries. One definition serves both sides — the reducer's twin `AgentPhase` is gone.

AssignAckArgs.description: `assign_ack`: whether the plugin took the payload.

attachments.description: Absolute paths of the files this delivery carries, in the order `text` names them. The client writes them before the assignment leaves, so every path here names a file that exists.

parent.description: Envelope of the task that caused this one, when downstream.

text.description:
The delivery text, rendered by the client's one template (`onlyne-client`'s `delivery` module).

A plugin injects these bytes and renders nothing of its own: the wording of a delivery is a contract (`AGENTS.md` §12), and v1 built it once per plugin — JavaScript here, Rust in the ACP backend — so the text a model read depended on which drive delivered it. The envelope still travels beside it, for the fields a plugin reports on rather than injects.

Body.description: Envelope payload: text plus at most one inline image.

head.description: One display line the sender names for this body, which a reader shows in place of a preview of the body's own text. `None` is the ordinary case: the body's text is the only content, and a store that keeps a one-line preview derives it from the text. A completion that carries its full result in `text` and a one-line summary separately sets this, so the summary is what a ledger shows rather than the first clusters of the result.

Capability.description: Optional plugin abilities. Absence of an entry is a declared gap: the host degrades and records a fault rather than assuming support.

oneOf.description: Bind a live process to a task via `session_register`.
Push lifecycle `report` frames.
Accept an injected payload through `assign`.
Honour `recycle` by tearing its own process down.
Answer `probe` with a fresh observation.
Emit `typing` indicators on the platform.
Enumerate real conversations during `register_channel`.
Keep session conversation in the runtime store so its process can be released and resumed.

Causality.description: Causality chain over one task family.

deadline.description: Wall-clock bound for the whole family.

family.description: The family's root task id. Every task handed on from one root carries the same family, which is what lets a supervisor read a whole run as one arc instead of walking `parent_task` links, and what `onlyne ledger` prints beside the hop. A root minted before this field existed names none, and the first child mints the family from its own parent.

hop.description: Hop count from the root task.

hop_budget.description: The hops this family may spend, set by whoever started it. A role reads it to learn whether it is the hop that keeps the task, which keeps that budget out of the task text.

labels.description: Free-form metadata the core carries and never interprets. Bounded by [`CAUSALITY_LABEL_MAX_ENTRIES`], [`CAUSALITY_LABEL_KEY_MAX_BYTES`], and [`CAUSALITY_LABEL_VALUE_MAX_BYTES`] at [`Envelope::validate`].

origin.description: The role this family reports home to, when the sender is not that role.

parent_task.description: The task that caused this one, when downstream.

task.description: Task family id, uuid v4, minted when the work is created.

ClusterMount.description: Where a sub-cluster's supervisor claims it speaks for another cluster.

role.description: The aggregate role name registered in the parent spec.

ConfigGetArgs.description: `config_get`: dotted key into the role's local config.

ControlOp.description: A command over an existing task.

oneOf.description: Tear the session down and release its slot.
Ask the owning client for a fresh probe of the resource.
Ask for the full lifecycle projection right now.
Abandon the task and settle it as cancelled.
Bring the task's live session to the front of its host.

Delivery.description: One delivered envelope plus its ledger handle.

DeliveryPhase.description: Intent delivery fact for the current turn exit: the delivery dimension of a session. `none` is the word for `NoIntent`, which is also its serde word.

DetachArgs.description: `detach`: the plugin leaves; the reason is recorded verbatim.

Envelope.description: The single message shape for the whole system.

admin.description: Set when the sender holds `admin = true` in the spec.

op_id.description:
Idempotency key: mandatory for Task, Completion, Control.

`None` is legal only for [`MsgKind::Note`], and [`Envelope::validate`] enforces that: a Task, Completion, or Control without a key is refused on the field `op_id`, so the retry the sender eventually makes dedups on one id.

A note that needs a durable row — the client queues every outbound envelope keyed by its `op_id` — is stamped once by the code that writes the row, and the stamped envelope is what gets stored and replayed (see `stamp_op_id` in `onlyne-client`). So the absent key here never means "mint one per attempt": a caller that generated a fresh id on every read would key each retry as a new send, and idempotence would silently stop existing. Keep `op_id` as received, and stamp before the first write.

ttl_ms.description: Notes expire; a queued note past its deadline is settled `expired`.

ErrorCode.description: The complete set of wire error codes, all lowercase with underscores.

oneOf.description: A field or argument failed a protocol rule.
The `op` name is unknown to this connection's vocabulary.
The spec forbids this sender for this target and kind.
No role by that name exists in the spec.
The recipient's client is not connected and the kind cannot queue.
This `op_id` was already accepted with an identical fingerprint.
This `op_id` was already accepted with a different fingerprint.
Handshake identity failed: unregistered key or bad signature.
Connected and registered, yet forbidden from this action.
The action needs `admin = true` in the spec.
A frame exceeded the negotiated byte ceiling.
A frame failed to decode.
Protocol revision outside the accepted range.
Ledger or runtime failure inside the daemon.

ErrorPayload.description: A wire error: closed code, human message, optional offending field.

GatewayMount.description: Gateway-side mount data carried in the same `hello` frame.

HandoffArgs.description:
`assign` payload: the envelope plus the role prose that frames it. One session handing its task on, as the plugin asks for it.

The family's own rules stay here: the host reads the task it holds, mints the child through [`Causality::child_of`], and lets the family id, the hop budget, the origin, the deadline, and the labels ride along. A plugin that built the child itself would have to reproduce every one of those rules.

The answer carries the child: `{ "task_id": "<uuid>", "hop": 3, "queued": true, "op_id": "<uuid>" }`.

image.description: One inline image, the same shape a task body carries.

task_id.description: The task the session is handing on; the child is minted under it.

uptime_s.description: Seconds since the gateway process started.

HelloAck.description: Everything the host answers a successful `hello` with (§5, §7).

delivered_tasks.description:
Tasks the host has already dispatched to a session of this role.

A plugin that says `hello` after a restart seeds its own delivery bookkeeping from this list, so a task the host already handed out is never injected twice. The list names task ids; it is always an array and empty when the host holds nothing to report.

host_capabilities.description: Capabilities the host itself will exercise against this plugin.

role.description: The role this connection is bound to.

session_id.description: Session id assigned or confirmed by the host.

version.description: Its own semver, recorded for fault triage.

HostOp.description: Host frames, in the direction host to plugin.

oneOf.description: Answer to `hello`, carrying the role's spec slice.
Hand this payload to the agent for the task.
Render and send this envelope on the platform (gateway mounts).
Ask for a fresh observation right now.
Tear the session down and release its slot.
Read one host config key.

Ask the plugin to hand one client-composed sentence to its agent input.

This is sent only to a plugin that declared `inject`; the client decides whether a drive can be nudged. The text is verbatim, and the plugin keeps no copy, composes none, and does not reset its turn bookkeeping. Its response claims only that the sentence was handed over.
The host is going away.

ImagePart.description: One inline image, carried base64 inside the envelope.

Lifecycle.description: Public lifecycle projection of a session, as published by the client that owns it.

Mount.description:
Plugin and gateway mount data, discriminated by [`MountKind`].

The mount names the configured instance the connection serves, and that is the identity the ACL and the routing use: `gateway` holds a `[[gateway]]` id and `role` holds a spec role name, both taken from the server's spec, because one plugin crate can back several configured instances with their own credentials, channels, and `[[route]]` bindings.

The program name travels in its own field. `HelloArgs::plugin` on this surface and `HandshakeArgs::agent` on a role connection name the crate that connected, which is the thing a protocol or version mismatch is about. Deriving the instance from the program would collapse the several-instances case.

The enum is untagged, so the wire form is the plan's own `hello` example at §7 line 298 — `"mount":{"role":"planner","session":"8b1c..."}` — with `kind` beside it in the same args object rather than nested under a tag.

Untagged matching is first-match-wins, so the variant order below is the disambiguation rule: `Agent`, then `Gateway`, then `Cluster`, then `Tools`, then `Admin`. Each payload denies unknown fields, and that guard is what makes the order safe to read rather than a silent mis-decode: `AgentMount` and `ClusterMount` both carry `role`, so without it a cluster mount would decode as an agent mount. A new field belongs to the earliest variant that owns it, and making one collide with an earlier variant's set is a wire change this list must be updated for.

A bare `Admin` mount serializes as JSON `null`; the sibling `kind` field is what identifies it.

anyOf.description: Admin tooling needs no mount data.

MountKind.description: Which side of the split a process mounts on.

oneOf.description: Agent plugin on a role client socket.
Platform gateway on the server socket.
ACP tool bridge on a role client socket.
Local operator tooling on the server socket.

MsgKind.description: Delivery intent and queueing class (decision D11, D10).

oneOf.description: Hand work to a role, creating or reusing a session.
Terminal receipt for a task.
Free text. Never queued, never creates a session.
Lifecycle command over a task: recycle, probe, snapshot, cancel.

The delivery ended waiting on something outside it.

A first-class result rather than a synonym for `Failed`: the ending rule settles a delivery whose session ended without a completion as blocked, and a board reads it as waiting rather than as failed.

PluginOp.description: Plugin and gateway frames, in the direction plugin to host.

oneOf.description: First frame on the connection.
A lifecycle observation for the reducer (§6).
Bind this process to a task and session.
Answer to [`HostOp::Assign`].
Submit an envelope for routing.
Hand the session's task on: the host mints one child of the family the session serves, queues it for `to`, and answers the child's task id and hop.
Inbound platform event (gateway mounts only).
Channel and conversation declarations (gateway mounts only).
Platform health (gateway mounts only).
Typing indicator for one conversation (gateway mounts only).
Stop receiving work; the plugin is leaving while its session continues.

Principal.description: Process-local identity of a message sender.

oneOf.description: A role in the cluster, optionally narrowed to one of its sessions.
An external IM conversation reached through a gateway.
A subordinate cluster, used by admin and aggregate reporting only.

RecoveryPhase.description: Recovery substate carried alongside an idle or draining session. `none` is the word for `NoRecovery`, which is also its serde word.

RecycleArgs.description: `recycle`: reason is mandatory so the ledger records the decision.

outcome.description: Settle the task with this outcome once the resource is gone.

RegisterChannelArgs.description: Channel declarations plus the optional conversation list.

conversations.description: Absent when the platform cannot enumerate conversations (§10.3).

RenderSendArgs.description: `render_send`: one envelope for the platform, plus the local correlation the gateway needs to answer it later.

conversation.description: Platform target the gateway must address.

gateway_ref.description: Opaque handle stored in the gateway's own table (§10.3).

reply_to.description: Platform-side id of the message being replied to, opaque to the host and decoded by the plugin that minted it. §7 line 304 is the inbound `deliver` frame whose envelope's `causality.reply_to` is the only place the id can travel, and the host copies it out while rendering, so a plugin never parses an envelope to thread a reply. Pairs with [`Self::gateway_ref`], which names the conversation.

Report.description:
The report envelope kinds a client pushes (§6, §7).

`cluster_ref` names the origin cluster on a relayed report, so a federated projection can say where it came from. Only the three state-carrying kinds hold it: `Fault` carries no projection, and a ninth optional field there would push `Report` and `ClientOp` from 192 to 224 bytes on the hot path.

`heartbeat` is the one frame that carries a session's state to the server. Two shapes travel under the same kind, and both are optional-skipped so neither writes a field the other has no use for: - the adapter's beat — a plugin telling its host it is alive — holds `observed` alone. The host reduces that tuple into the session row it keeps, and `session_id`/`projection` stay absent. - the client's publish to the server holds `projection`, the whole [`SessionProjection`] it stores for the task, beside the same `observed` tuple so the two never disagree. The server mirrors that projection verbatim; `session_id` names the row it belongs to.

A beat holding no `projection` is liveness only: the server keeps the working/running/pending/attached tuple it has always inferred from it.

oneOf.description: The ready barrier passed; the server may now deliver the payload.
Liveness plus, on the client-to-server path, the whole projection.

projection.description: The client's full session projection, published for the server to mirror. Absent on a liveness-only beat.

session_id.description: The session the published projection belongs to. Absent on the adapter's beat, which names no session.

oneOf.description: Terminal result for a task; `head` is the summary the ledger keeps.

details.description: The full result, delivered verbatim to the next hop and the originator.

files.description: Absolute paths of the files the result names.

oneOf.description: Something needs a supervisor decision. The server records and forwards.

ResBody.description:
The response body carried by [`Frame::Res`].

`ok = true` carries `data` and `ok = false` carries `error`, and neither may omit its own half. The one pair is the duplicate `op_id` replay: `ok = false` with an `error` naming `duplicate` and the replayed receipt in `data`, which is the shape `docs/v1-PLAN.md` case 3 at line 502 compares byte for byte.

ResourcePhase.description: Backend resource fact (pane / tab / terminal handle): the resource dimension of a session.

ServerInfo.description: Cluster identity handed out at handshake.

SessionProjection.description: The full projection the client publishes for one session (§10 `sessions`).

observed.description: Raw reducer observation, retained for repair and forensics.

SessionRegisterArgs.description: `session_register`: bind a live process to a task.

ToolsMount.description:
ACP tool bridge mount data carried in the same `hello` frame.

The token is the binding: the client mints it for one `(role, session, generation)` and records that association, so the bridge never supplies a role of its own. A caller that could name a role here could speak for a session it never held.

TypingArgs.description: `typing`: platform typing indicator for one conversation. `on` starts the indicator and `false` stops it, which is the pair a platform API exposes.
